claims.value: A pyramidal cell with abundant mitochondria and a network of microvilli-lined secretory canaliculi, it secretes hydrochloric acid into the stomach lumen and produces intrinsic factor, which is essential for vitamin B12 absorption.
claims.quote: This cell is characterized by its pyramidal shape, abundant mitochondria, and a complex network of secretory canaliculi lined with microvilli. It secretes hydrochloric acid into the stomach lumen and produces intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption.

claims.value: Relatively large and among the body's most highly differentiated epithelial cells, parietal cells sit mainly in the middle region of the gastric glands and produce both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.
claims.quote: Located primarily in the middle region of the gastric glands are parietal cells, which are among the most highly differentiated of the body’s epithelial cells. These relatively large cells produce both hydrochloric acid (HCl) and intrinsic factor.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The hydrochloric acid these cells produce gives the stomach contents their high acidity (pH 1.5 to 3.5) and is needed to activate the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin.
claims.quote: These relatively large cells produce both hydrochloric acid (HCl) and intrinsic factor. HCl is responsible for the high acidity (pH 1.5 to 3.5) of the stomach contents and is needed to activate the protein-digesting enzyme, pepsin.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Parietal cells secrete hydrogen and chloride ions, which combine in the lumen to form hydrochloric acid, the primary acidic component of stomach juices.
claims.quote: Another cell type—parietal cells—secrete hydrogen and chloride ions, which combine in the lumen to form hydrochloric acid, the primary acidic component of the stomach juices.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Gastrin stimulates parietal cells in the stomach mucosa to secrete gastric acid.
claims.quote: Gastrin stimulates the secretion of gastric acid by the parietal cells of the stomach mucosa.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Histamine, made by the stomach mucosa when food is in the stomach, stimulates parietal cells to release HCl.

tier1.text: An epithelial cell of the stomach that is part of the fundic gastric gland. This cell is characterized by its pyramidal shape, abundant mitochondria, and a complex network of secretory canaliculi lined with microvilli. It secretes hydrochloric acid into the stomach lumen and produces intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption.
